text: Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere dissolves in rain water making it acidic. When this water passes
through limestone containing calcium carbonate, it forms solutions of calcium hydrogen carbonate.
In this experiment, you will determine the concentration of hydrogen carbonate ions in a solution by
titration with hydrochloric acid.
FB 1 is 0.100 mol dm hydrochloric acid, HCl.
FB 2 contains an unknown concentration of hydrogen carbonate ions, HCO .

text: As well as hydrogen carbonate ions, water that has passed through rocks also contains a range of
metal ions such as Ca . The presence of Ca ions leads to the water forming scum with certain
types of soap. Soluble metal carbonates can be added to remove these ions. One such soluble
carbonate is M CO3.10H O.
In this experiment you will heat a sample of the carbonate salt to remove the water of crystallisation
and leave the anhydrous salt, M CO . By working out how much water was lost you will be able to
calculate the relative formula mass of M CO3.10H O and hence identify M.
FB 3 is the hydrated salt, M CO3.10H O.
